ns2:section.sectionText: This course will cover a number of statistical techniques that are relevant to astrophysical studies. These include robust statistics, regression, model building and hypotheses testing, MCMC methods, parameter estimation, time series analysis, clustering and dimensionality reduction, supervised machine learning, and hierarchical modeling. These techniques are used in almost every paper you'll read. The goal of this course is to ensure you understand how these techniques work, and what their implicit assumptions are, so that you can make informed modeling choices with real data. You'll also learn how to use the tools that implement these techniques, best practices for writing code and version control, and how to craft detailed analyses into a readable telescope or grant proposal.
